title: Why Yawns Are Contagious (Try Not To Yawn)
description:
Yawns spread from person to person, and even to dogs. Here is what science knows about why.

SOURCES:
- Provine, R. R. (1986). Yawning as a stereotyped action pattern and releasing stimulus. Ethology, 72(2), 109-122
- Platek, S. M., Critton, S. R., Myers, T. E., & Gallup, G. G. (2003). Contagious yawning: the role of self-awareness and mental state attribution. Cognitive Brain Research, 17(2), 223-227
- Millen, A., & Anderson, J. R. (2011). Neither infants nor toddlers catch yawns from their mothers. Biology Letters, 7(3), 440-442
- Joly-Mascheroni, R. M., Senju, A., & Shepherd, A. J. (2008). Dogs catch human yawns. Biology Letters, 4(5), 446-448
- Norscia, I., & Palagi, E. (2011). Yawn contagion and empathy in Homo sapiens. PLoS ONE, 6(12): e28472.
- Gallup, A. C., & Gallup, G. G. (2007). Yawning as a brain cooling mechanism. Evolutionary Psychology, 5(1), 92-101

Educational content, not medical advice. If you feel unusually tired all the time, talk to a doctor.
